text:
anya: quick idea  small CLI for concise deploy annotations that also creates a draft PR for release notes by default. goal: one-liner intent + automatic note blob so product/ops don't need to chase context

miguel: show me the flags you'd want

anya: prototype command:
```
/deploy annotate \n  --idempotent \n  --sig "llm-encoder-cost-opt" \n  --pin "model=encoder-3.2.0" \n  --window "in2h/2h"   # shorthand for start=now+2h duration=2h
  --notes-template short  # uses built-in YAML template if omitted\n  --auto-rollback 3%:5m  # threshold:3% over 5m window\n  --notify team\n```

deploy-bot: draft created: annot-3499004321 (preview) -> "sig: llm-encoder-cost-opt | pin: encoder-3.2.0 | window: in2h/2h | auto-rollback:3%/5m"

ops-oncall: can the shorthand also accept calendar ranges? e.g. `tomorrow/1h` or `2026-03-24T09:00/2026-03-24T11:00`

anya: yes, parser accepts RFC3339 ranges, relative shorthands (`inXh`, `tomorrow`) and `calendar:team-release` alias to tie to our shared change windows calendar

miguel: about PRs  if template is used we want a small YAML blob in the PR body so our release-bot can scan it. example YAML: 
```yaml
sig: llm-encoder-cost-opt
summary: tweak to KV cache behaviour to reduce tail cost
checks:
  - perf-smoke: pass
  - canary: 15k reqs <3% err
  - rollback: auto(3%/5m) available
notes_link: https://git.redwood/release-notes/3499
```

release-sheriff-bot: canary hookup available: `--canary-source=prometheus:embed-enc-canary` and we can optionally `--canary-metric=error_rate`

ops-oncall: edge case  what if someone uses `--pin model=encoder@^3`? we should make pin mode explicit by default (append vs replace)

anya: default `--pin-mode=append` to keep pin history, `--pin-mode=replace` for explicit overrides. CLI will warn on ranges unless `--force-range` supplied

miguel: UX request  show a compact Slack preview with two buttons: [Open PR] [Cancel]. If user clicks Open PR the bot runs preflight hooks (lint, smoke, canary warmup check) then creates draft PR. If hooks fail it posts summary with failure tags

deploy-bot: implemented prototype UI. example preview message: "llm-encoder-cost-opt | encoder-3.2.0 | window: tomorrow 09:00-11:00 | auto-rollback: 3%/5m" with interactive buttons

ops-oncall: also add `--quiet-on-success` so routine small pins (hotfixes) don't ping the whole channel. by default `notify=team`

anya: good call. final flags list I'm putting in the RFC: `--sig, --pin, --pin-mode, --window, --auto-rollback, --canary-source, --canary-metric, --notes-template, --no-pr, --notify, --quiet-on-success, --dry-run, --idempotent`

miguel: I'll draft the RFC and include a mini state-machine for actions: preview -> user click -> preflight -> create PR -> annotate deploy metadata -> optional auto-rollback monitor. will add tests for idempotency and range warnings

anya: assigning @release-sheriff-bot to verify prometheus hooks and @ops-oncall to sanity-check calendar aliases. planning to land small bot patch + release-notes PR creator, then enable feature flag for beta group

ops-oncall: ack, will validate calendar tokens and timezone handling (UTC vs local team tz)

miguel: nice. once RFC open we'll pair on the preflight checklist and add a small E2E that simulates a failing canary and ensures auto-rollback triggers only when enabled

anya: thanks all  I'll open the RFC PR in ~30m with the example YAML and screenshots of the Slack preview

migrated-bot-note: this thread will be linked from the RFC under `design/deploy-annotator`
